title: Root-cause the with-SDK vs. flat-context accuracy gap with real evidence, not assumption
summary: Instrument the retrieval-quality suite to log actual search() results (content, order, distance) per failing question; confirm or refute BENCHMARKS.md's existing 'missing turns' hypothesis before any fix lands.
description:
Run B (project-management/BENCHMARKS.md, llama3.1:8b judge, nomic-embed-text, n=50, seed=42) shows with-SDK scoring below the flat-context baseline on extraction (-10.0%), multi_session (-30.0%), temporal_reasoning (-30.0%), and knowledge_update (-10.0%). The report's existing analysis guesses the cause is `search()` "returning only one of the two relevant turns" at top_k=5 — but every multi_session/temporal_reasoning/knowledge_update question in benchmarks/retrieval_quality/dataset.py plants exactly 2 turns total in its scope, and top_k defaults to 5 (2 <= 5), so both turns should be retrieved every time. That existing hypothesis needs to be checked against real data, not repeated as fact.

Add debug instrumentation to `run_retrieval_quality()` (benchmarks/retrieval_quality/run.py) that, for every question the judge marks INCORRECT, logs: the full ordered `results` list from `store.working.search()` (content + rank + distance if available), the `retrieved_context` string actually handed to the judge, and the corresponding flat-context baseline string for the same question id. Re-run `--suite retrieval --baseline` at the same seed/config as Run B and inspect every failing question in the four negative-delta categories.

Specifically test these candidate root causes, don't assume one:
1. **Recall** — is a relevant turn actually missing from `results` (confirms/refutes the existing BENCHMARKS.md theory)?
2. **Ordering** — `store.working.search()` orders results by vector distance to the query, not chronological/session order, while `run_baseline()`'s flat context is always in original session order (`benchmarks/retrieval_quality/run.py`: compare the two join expressions directly). For temporal_reasoning ("before the promotion") and knowledge_update ("CURRENT ... language"), an out-of-chronological-order presentation is a plausible confounder distinct from missing recall — check whether incorrect answers correlate with reordering.
3. **Judge non-determinism** — local Ollama models are not necessarily deterministic run-to-run at default sampling settings; re-run the same failing questions 2-3x and see if the verdict flips.

Before starting: read DECISIONS.md in full — this is a diagnostic story, land no code fix here beyond the temporary logging instrumentation (remove or gate it behind `--debug` before finishing, don't leave permanent noisy logging on the hot path). Before finishing: append a dated DECISIONS.md entry with the confirmed root cause per category (recall vs. ordering vs. judge noise vs. something else found), and update the 'Analysis — what the delta tells us' section of BENCHMARKS.md's Run B if the existing hypothesis turns out to be wrong or incomplete. This story's findings determine the scope of BENCH-2/BENCH-3/BENCH-4 below — don't start those until this lands.

comments.text:
BENCH-1 complete. Root cause confirmed with --debug instrumentation across 3 diagnostic runs (seed=42, ollama/nomic-embed-text, llama3.1:8b judge, n=10/category).

The BENCHMARKS.md hypothesis ('search() returning only one of two relevant turns at top_k=5') is WRONG. Every failing question showed results (0 retrieved) — zero results, not partial recall.

Confirmed root cause: ORC-2 chunk-path routing bug in search() auto-detect (base.py:1370-1371). MemoryStore is built with enable_chunking=True and an embedding_provider, so chunk_repo is not None. search() auto-detects effective_search_chunks = (chunk_repo is not None) = True, routing ALL searches through _search_via_chunks() which queries only memory_chunks. Benchmark turns are short sentences (~50-120 chars) far below chunk_threshold=2000 -- remember() stores embeddings on the parent row and writes nothing to memory_chunks. Result: _search_via_chunks() finds nothing, returns [], judge sees empty context, marks INCORRECT.

Candidate 1 (recall): CONFIRMED as proximate cause -- zero results returned for every failing question.
Candidate 2 (ordering): NOT a factor -- no results to reorder.
Candidate 3 (judge non-determinism): CONFIRMED as secondary variance -- plus or minus 2-4 questions per run (~plus or minus 8% overall) with no retrieval change across runs.

Fix for BENCH-2: correct search() auto-detect in base.py to fall back to standard parent-embedding path when chunk search returns nothing; or pass search_chunks=False explicitly in run_retrieval_quality(). Ordering hypothesis refuted. See DECISIONS.md BENCH-1 entry for full call chain.
